PRECONDITION TO ADD TO THE RUNBOOK - assert src vs build parity before a walk. Pro blocks register from MVS_PRO_DIR . 'build/blocks/' (includes/Blocks/BlockRegistrar.php:73-80), and build/ is gitignored (wpmediaverse-pro/.gitignore:23). It is refreshed only by an explicit build, so a clean git tree says nothing about what the site actually renders and the walked site can silently lag the source. That is exactly what happened this cycle: the pro-document-embed fix was correct in src/ from the first re-verify, but build/ still held the pre-fix file, so the row read as a broken fix for a whole round trip. Packaging does run grunt build -> npm run build:blocks, so the zip would have shipped the correct code - the risk is not a bad release, it is QA certifying a build the release does not contain, in either direction. Suggested check at the top of Global preconditions: for each src/blocks/*/render.php, compare against build/blocks/<slug>/render.php and STOP if any differ, the same way fixture cleanup failing is treated as a release blocker.

RUNBOOK MAINTENANCE DEBT - the runbook's own rule is that every customer-visible fix ships with a matching D row in the same PR. Four fixes verified across these runs have no D row yet: the grid query-budget batching (cache_users, one grouped COUNT, and dropping get_post_type from the typed-index privacy path), the Explore bulk-delete confirm-overlay context, the tag-autocomplete await, and the pro-document-embed editor notice. The bulk-delete fix is partly covered by C.member.bulk-trash-restore-delete; the tag autocomplete has no runbook coverage at all on either surface. The pro-document-embed case argues for a D row that asserts the notice renders from the BUILT file, not just that the source contains it.

RE-BASELINE THE QUERY ROW - C.member.grid-render-query-budget / D.grid-render-n-plus-1 still read 'under 6 DB queries per page', which no longer describes what is being protected. After the fix the cost is a fixed per-page floor that does not grow with tile count: mvs/media-grid measured in its own cold process at perPage 1 = 12 queries, perPage 12 = 13, perPage 24 = 15, so the marginal cost is about 0.13 queries per tile (was about 2.45) and 11 extra tiles cost 1 query (was 27). Real /media/ page: 105 total queries for 12 tiles (was 117), delta against a 1-tile tag page 14 (was 25). Rewrite the row as a per-page floor (about 12-13 on this fixture) plus a marginal per-tile ceiling, since the flat curve is the real assertion. Rendered output after the fix: 12 tiles, 36695 bytes, md5 864d7d596be16588198ee1cfb37aff92. The 'byte-identical to pre-fix' claim could not be independently confirmed because the pre-fix output was not hashed during the original walk.

OBSERVATION, NOT A GATE FAILURE - mvs_media_index.comment_count is a read-never-written column. Filed as Basecamp card 10320950705. The runbook does not require a gate failure for this class: the nearest rule (C.admin.settings-readers) explicitly prescribes 'flag them as from-origin observations', the column violates no C or D contract that was walked (C.member.reactions-favorites-comments' own contract - comments post, wp_comments-scoped - passed), and the counter-sync line lives in B1, which is skipped on this site. There is no customer-visible symptom: no render path in includes/, templates/ or src/ prints comment_count, so nothing displays a wrong number. Evidence: one approved comment on media 67569 left reaction_count correctly at 1 and comment_count at 0. Either wire the counter or drop the column.

RUNBOOK CORRECTIONS the next editor should apply (verified against 2.5.1 code, not defects): (1) C.anon.single-media claims /p/<media_id>/ is the canonical MVS URL - it is not. /p/([0-9]+) is BuddyNext's route (buddynext/includes/Core/PageRouter.php:2358, -> bn_hub=post), so /p/<mvs media id>/ correctly 404s. MVS's own route is /media/<slug>/ -> mvs_media_slug, and on this site BuddyNext redirects it via the documented mvs_single_media_redirect filter. The native MVS single page was verified by neutralising that filter for one request and returns 200 with h1, og:image, og:title, twitter:card, a 200 image/webp asset and 6 reaction buttons. (2) E.group-dm cites POST/GET /mvs-pro/v1/groups/{id}/messages - that route does not exist; group creation is /mvs-pro/v1/groups (a group IS a conversation) and messaging goes through Free's /mvs/v1/conversations/{id}/messages, which works end to end. A non-member gets 404, not the 403 the row states. (3) The Fixture cleanup block deletes mvs_reports WHERE reason LIKE 'smoke-%', but reason is an enum (spam|harassment|nudity|violence|copyright|misinformation|other) so that clause can never match - the free-text marker belongs in the details column. (4) C.member.video-poster-fallback names PosterService::is_ffmpeg_available() - PosterService has only dir(), stage_bytes() and stage_client_frame(), and no ffmpeg helper exists in Free at all. (5) D.documents-privacy-vocabulary asserts PRIVACY_VALUES is exactly private/members/public - it is now private/space/members/public, with space added for space drives. The bug the row guards is gone: nothing offers 'unlisted', and POST with unlisted or restricted both answer 400 mvs_document_privacy_invalid. (6) C.member.lightbox-edit-modal says the Edit cog appears ONLY on /my-media/ cards - in 2.5.1 an owner also sees it in the Explore lightbox for their own media. That is not a leak: for a non-owner the action computes display:none, and PUT and DELETE both answer 403 mvs_forbidden. The row's wording should be owner-scoped, not surface-scoped. (7) C.member.bulk-trash-restore-delete describes bulk Move to Trash plus a Trashed filter on /my-media/ - the member dashboard bulk bar offers Set privacy, Add to album, Add tags and Delete. Trash/Restore/Delete-permanently live on admin All Media, which is the surface this walk used.

UX gaps observed but not recorded as gate failures, for the maintainer's judgement: (a) admin Documents single view accepts a save with an empty title and reports 'Document updated.' while silently discarding the change - data is safe (the DB kept the previous title) but the feedback is wrong; (b) an admin All Media bulk submit with zero rows selected produces no notice at all - not destructive, but the runbook asks for a friendly error; (c) the lightbox edit modal exposes title, description, privacy and 'Update URL slug' but no allow_download control, although OPTIONS on /mvs/v1/media/{id} declares allow_download as editable; (d) POST /mvs/v1/media returns 201 after silently downgrading a requested privacy to the site default when mvs_allow_user_privacy is off, while PUT on the same resource returns mvs_privacy_locked - the create path should be as loud as the update path; (e) the collections picker's per-row 'Saving.../Saved' feedback could not be observed at 600ms or 3100ms after ticking, though the write landed and the Collections tab correctly showed '1 item' with a real cover thumbnail.
